body:
maria: I uploaded an nsys + perfetto capture for the long-seq perf regression. behavior looks different when seq_len > 2048 - kernel fanout changes and KV reads spike. link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?url=redwood/trace-2934012345

maria: short summary — steady-state throughput drops ~22% on A100 when request sequences hit tails; HBM BW shows intermittent 1.6x spikes.

tom: saw the same on my local run. kernel selection toggles between fast_matmul_v2 and matmul_fallback around step 87 of the trace. that aligns with a sudden rise in L2 read stalls.

ali: can you paste the nsys CLI you used? I'll repro.

maria: ran: ```nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn --output=kv-wave-2934 ./run_infer --model /models/opt-13b --seq 3072 --batch 1``` captured CUDA kernel timelines + NVTX markers. also recorded CUPTI memcpy counters.

perf-bot: nsys summary: total_gpu_time: 0.98s, cublas_time: 0.44s, memcpy_h2d: 0.02s, memcpy_d2h: 0.01s, kernel_preempt: 3 events

jess: interesting — our kernel selector has a heuristic: if avg_seq_len > 1536 choose fast_matmul_v2, else matmul_fallback. maybe the runtime mis-estimates the active seq window because of batching heuristic microbursts.

indra: I inspected KV cache timeline in perfetto. There are short windows where KV read rate doubles and then the allocator triggers an eviction scan. trace snippet: ```KV_READS/sec  ->  200k  at t=11.3s  then 400k at t=11.32s``` eviction latency concurrently jumps to 6ms.

tom: does that map to HBM bandwidth hotspots?

maria: yes — HBM utilization graph shows baseline ~280 GB/s but during the little spike it hits ~420 GB/s. I think microbatch tails cause many concurrent KV lookups hitting cold pages and causing DMA stalls.

ali: Could be a batching heuristic bug where we try to coalesce requests across variable-length inputs and end up routing cold KV pages to a different kernel that has larger gather op. The larger gather triggers more scatter-gather memory traffic and changes kernel choice.

jess: action items I suggest: 1) add an NVTX marker around the batching decision to correlate with kernel dispatch, 2) add an instrumentation counter for 'kv_cold_hit_rate' in runtime, 3) capture a short mempipe trace with CUPTI to confirm DMA stall metrics.

maria: +1. I already added NVTX->BATCH_DECISION and NVTX->KV_LOOKUP markers in the next run. attaching the perfetto snippet where you can see the NVTX markers aligned with kernel switches.

nsys-bot: note: next run scheduled with --output=kv-wave-2934-2. Also include env REDWOOD_BATCHER_DEBUG=1 for extra logging.

tom: small repro note — reducing microbatching window from 50ms to 30ms removes the spike in my env. that suggests our batching timeout amplifies the tail overlap.

indra: to confirm root cause we should try: a) force kernel selector to prefer matmul_fallback even for long seq (cheap toggle) b) replay trace with KV cache pinned (no eviction) c) run with quantized kernels to see if access pattern changes.

ali: I'll try (a) and (b) today. if forcing matmul_fallback recovers throughput then kernel selection + memory pattern is the culprit.

maria: uploaded the nvprof style timeline export and a short flamegraph for the hot thread. keys: high L2 miss ratio during fast_matmul_v2, and a pronounced spike in cudaMemcpyAsync wait time.

jess: def can be kernel choice interacting badly with KV page alignment causing unaligned DMA batches. possible mitigation: align KV pages to 2MB boundaries and prefer an SG-friendly gather kernel when page crosses boundary.

tom: timeline note — the kernel swap always happens right after a dynamic batching merge. suspect the merge aggregates tails causing wider vector lengths so the selector sees an 'effective longer sequence' and flips kernel.

maria: repro checklist appended in trace comments. I'll create a small test that simulates three variable-length inputs that collide to replicate the exact NVTX sequence.

ali: quick test results: forcing selector to fallback recovered 17% perf. pinning KV prevented HBM spikes but didn't fully restore baseline — so both eviction noise and kernel choice contribute.

jess: good evidence. let's prioritize: 1) patch selector to be more conservative when batch contains variable-length tails, 2) add a soft cap that prevents switching to fast_matmul_v2 if pending KV eviction backlog > threshold, 3) follow up on page alignment mitigation as a longer term fix.

maria: I'll open a PR with a conservative selector flag + NVTX markers and attach the perfetto traces to the PR for review.

maria: thanks everyone — great debugging session. will post updated traces in this thread when the patched build finishes profiling. :white_check_mark:
